Subject: POC MAP checkpoint — acceptance criteria audit & blocker roster

Hi Sam / Helix team,

Thanks for the sync last week. Per our MAP cadence I attached the latest MAP workbook (HLX_MAP_v1.3.xlsx) — I ran an acceptance-criteria audit on the evaluation plan tab and flagged gaps where we need clarified pass/fail definitions for inference latency, false-positive rate on redaction rules, and end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) with realistic payloads.

At a high level:
- Current trial window: Aug 16–Sept 3 (as discussed).
- Key acceptance gates we need finalized:
  1) Latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms for 2k prompt-length distribution (owner: Redwood runtime)
  2) Data handling: redaction verification per Helix PII rules (owner: Helix QA)
  3) Quality: task-specific F1 >= 0.82 on the supplied eval set (owner: Helix / Redwood co-run)

Immediate asks:
1) Can Sam confirm who on your side will be owner for the redaction verification tests?
2) Procurement: any procurement-specific acceptance language we should include in the MAP before the trial starts?
3) Internal: Priyom, can you capture the exact test harness we’ll run for latency and add instructions to the TestPlan PDF?

I pulled together a short blockers roster in the workbook (blocked / mitigations column) — highlights:
- Data access: Helix sandbox credentials required (owner: Helix)
- SOC2 evidence request: procurement asked for a summary of controls (action: Mateo to coordinate)
- Network egress rules for VPC peering during the trial window

Next steps: I propose a 30-min checkpoint on Aug 17 to finalize owners and delivery dates. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Mateo — this is helpful. Quick answers: we’ll own the redaction verification on the Helix QA side, I’ll loop in Priya (Procurement) for contract language.

A few clarifying questions:
- For the latency gate, is the 2k prompt-length an average or maximum? Our evaluation will include both short and long prompts.
- On the F1 threshold: can Redwood provide the reference script you’ll use to compute F1 so we can run locally and verify?

Procurement note (cc): Priya, we typically need SOC2 evidence and a short IaaS diagram showing where logs land. Can Redwood share a top-line controls summary?

Sam / team — quick technical notes to address the asks:
1) Latency gate: the 2k figure is the maximum prompt length we plan to include in the 95p measurement. In practice, we’ll split runs into short (<256 tokens), med (256–1024), and long (1024–2048) buckets and compute both per-bucket and combined 95p. I will add the exact harness commands to POC_TestPlan_v2.pdf (see attachment).
2) F1 computation: I’ll push the evaluation script into the shared drive (link in the MAP workbook) and include a reproducible docker run line so Helix can run locally.
3) Network/VPC: For peering we need an IP allowlist from Helix infra.

Blocker notes (owner suggestions):
- Sandbox creds (owner: Helix infra)
- SOC2 summary (owner: Mateo)
- Egress rules / firewall (owner: Helix infra)

I’ll update the MAP workbook with test harness commands and expected artifact locations.

—Priyom

Thanks everyone — quick status update before our checkpoint tomorrow: 
- Updated HLX_MAP_v1.3.xlsx and uploaded POC_TestPlan_v2.pdf to the shared drive (link: https://docs.redwood.com/drive/HLX/POC_MAP_v1.3).
- Deliverables assigned:
  * Redaction verification checklist: Grace (ETA Aug 14) — in progress
  * Latency harness & eval script: Priyom (ETA Aug 15) — uploaded to drive
  * SOC2 controls summary + log retention note: Mateo (ETA Aug 18) — I’ll share a one-page summary and a network diagram for procurement.
  * Sandbox creds / VPC allowlist: action required from Helix infra
- Open blocker roster (from workbook): Sandbox creds (blocking latency runs), Procurement redlines (blocking final MAP), VPC egress rules (blocking remote tests).

Proposed conflict-resolution language for the MAP: 
"If an evaluation run identifies a trade-off between 'acceptable performance' metrics (for example, reduced latency vs. lowered task-specific quality), the parties shall prioritize task-specific quality (F1) for go/no-go decisions unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing. Any exception must be documented in the MAP sign-off appendix and signed by both parties' program leads'"

I’ll send a calendar invite for Aug 18, 10:00am PT to finalize the outstanding owners and procurement asks. Please review the updated workbook before the call.

Regards,
Mateo
